sources.summary: Official notice of the Universitätsstadt Gießen, signed by the Magistrat on 2 October 2026: the city council adopted Bebauungsplan GI 05/23 "Katzenfeld" as a by-law in its session of 27 August 2026 (and the 20th amendment of the land-use plan on 25 June 2026, approved by the Regierungspräsidium Gießen on 16 September 2026); with publication of this notice the Bebauungsplan enters into force under § 10(3) BauGB, and the plan documents with their Begründung are available for inspection and online.
sources.date_semantics: The notice is signed 2 October 2026; the city's Bekanntmachungen page lists it under 05.10.2026 (de-hesse-p1-giessen-bekanntmachungen-listing), the same day the zusammenfassende Erklärung gives for the publication of legal force, so the plan is in force from 5 October 2026. The notice names the plan, not the data centre; the plan's legend, textual provisions and zusammenfassende Erklärung (context sources) designate its Sondergebiet for a data centre. The local capture file name carries an erroneous 20261010 label; the listing date is 05.10.2026. Personal names in the document are not reproduced.

sources.title: Universitätsstadt Gießen: Zusammenfassende Erklärung nach § 10a BauGB zum Bebauungsplanverfahren GI 05/23 "Katzenfeld"
sources.summary: The statement accompanying the in-force plan lists the procedure (initiation 20.12.2018; early participation 2024; draft resolution 18.09.2025; public display 02.10.-10.11.2025; renewed limited participation 22.07.-07.08.2026; Satzungsbeschluss 27.08.2026; Ausfertigung 02.10.2026; publication of legal force 05.10.2026) and states that the plan opens a roughly 6 ha Gewerbegebiet and a roughly 6 ha Sondergebiet for a data centre within a plan area of about 16.6 ha, next to the Gießen-Nord substation. It notes that the data centre's emergency generators will require a separate Federal Immission Control Act procedure and that waste heat is to be fed into the Stadtwerke Gießen district-heating network.

sources.title: Universitätsstadt Gießen: Bebauungsplan GI 05/23 "Katzenfeld" — Begründung (in-force version)
sources.summary: The explanatory statement records that Revikon (Gießen) bought about two thirds of the plan area from the former owners and has acted since 2018 as developer and Erschließungsträgerin; that the Magistrat aims to use an area of about 6 ha for a data centre of about 65 MW total power intake (5.94 ha Sondergebiet Rechenzentrum), supplied from the 110 kV network at the adjacent Gießen-Nord substation; that no data-centre operator had been selected by the July 2026 participation step; and lists the cadastral parcels in Gemarkung Gießen Fluren 30, 31 and 32 within the 16.6 ha plan area bounded by the K 28 (Krofdorfer Straße), the flood dike and the Weilburger Grenze path. Soil works are expected from autumn 2026.

sources.attribution: Bezirksamt Hamburg-Mitte - Fachamt Bauprüfung; Transparenzportal Hamburg
sources.summary: Building permit GZ M-BP-2262-2025 dated Hamburg, 20 July 2026, issued by the Bezirksamt Hamburg-Mitte, Fachamt Bauprüfung, in the procedure under section 62 HBauO (application received 31 October 2025). Under section 72 HBauO it grants permission to carry out the new build of two data centres with generator platforms and eight car parking spaces in Gemarkung Hamm Marsch (address, block and parcel number redacted for publication). It is granted on site plan no. DE-IPHH4-BA-E0-INV-LA-M-52000 of 30 September 2025, cites the planning basis (Baustufenplan Hamm Marsch, industrial area) and preliminary decision M-BP-864-2024, and includes a tree-protection permit for 14 trees, among them trees on the embankment to the Mittelkanal that must give way to the two data centres. The building class is 5 and the buildings have four full storeys. A suspensive condition provides that the corresponding construction works may begin only after a supplementary decision on structural stability has been issued, and felling requires prior species-protection clearance. The permit lapses if execution does not begin within three years.
sources.date_semantics: The permit is dated 20 July 2026; the Transparenzportal dataset page (separate source) gives the publication date 29 July 2026, used as published_at and as the observation date of the issued permit. sources.title: Portus Data Centers: Portus Data Centers announces planned delivery of new Hamburg site (IPHH4)
sources.summary: Portus announces the planned availability of its new data centre IPHH4 on the IPHH Internet Port Hamburg Wendenstrasse campus, adjacent to the existing IPHH3 data centre at the main Wendenstrasse location; two infrastructures of 6.4 MW each (12.8 MW total IT load), 6,380 m2 white space (3,190 m2 per building), 20.3 MVA grid connection, design PUE of 1.2 or under. sources.title: EPA Industrial Emissions review licence P1186-02, Amazon Data Services Ireland Limited, Clonshaugh Business and Technology Park, Dublin 17 (final determination, sealed 24 September 2026)
sources.summary: The Agency's decision under section 90(2) of the EPA Act grants Amazon Data Services Ireland Limited (CRO 390566) an industrial emissions review licence for activity class 2.1 at Clonshaugh Business and Technology Park, Dublin 17, given under seal on 24 September 2026 in lieu of licence P1186-01. Its introduction states that the company currently operates a data storage facility there under licence P1186-01; that the currently licensed installation consists of three two-storey data storage buildings (Buildings X, Y and W) and ancillary elements; and that the review extends the installation to two further two-storey data storage buildings (Buildings U and V). The installation has 52 back-up generators (diesel or HVO), is supplied from the national grid in normal operation and discharges storm water to the Santry River via the park network. Schedule B lists the 52 generator stacks (A3-1 to A3-52) by Irish Grid reference.
sources.date_semantics: Sealed and posted to LEAP on 24 September 2026 (publication date); the newspaper notice followed on 1-2 October. The introduction's present-tense statement of current operation is read as of the licence date. The introduction says it is not part of the licence; it is the Agency's own description of the installation. It states no IT capacity, no opening date and no status for Buildings U and V beyond their inclusion.

sources.summary: CX Tech Limited says it has today submitted an application for Planning Permission in Principle for the proposed CX Technology Campus at the former Chapelcross nuclear power station site near Annan, Dumfries and Galloway: a net-zero operational technology campus of eight data-centre buildings of about 120 MW each (about 1 GW), up to 162,000 m2 of data-centre floorspace, a dedicated training centre and associated infrastructure, with an Environmental Impact Assessment, buildings of up to 40 m, closed-loop air cooling and fossil-free backup generation.
